chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from the one who mentioned it, from Aban, from Muhammad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Whatever is from different foodstuffs, or goods, or something of the things that differ in quality, there is no problem with selling it, two similar (portions) for one, hand to hand. As for respite (on credit), then it is not valid.

key_terms.طَعَامٍ: Foodstuffs, specifically referring to commodities like dates, grains, etc., used in fiqh of trade.
key_terms.فَلَا تَصْلُحُ: Then it is not valid, indicating the invalidity of the transaction under the condition of deferment.
key_terms.مُخْتَلِفٍ: Different, referring to varying qualities or grades within the same category of goods.
key_terms.مِثْلَيْنِ بِمِثْلٍ: Two similar (portions) for one, a key phrase indicating the exchange of unequal quantities of the same commodity type.
key_terms.نَظِرَةً: Respite or deferment, referring to credit sales where delivery or payment is delayed.
key_terms.يَداً بِيَدٍ: Hand to hand, denoting immediate exchange without delay.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling different qualities of the same food item on credit in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the application of the 'like-for-like' (mithl bi-mithl) principle in riba al-fadl, distinguishing between homogeneous goods where equality is required and heterogeneous goods where quantity may vary. It emphasizes that while immediate exchange (yadan bi-yad) allows for differing amounts in non-homogeneous items, any element of deferment (nasi'ah) renders the transaction invalid, a key distinction in Shia fiqh regarding commodity trading.
